title: After the Permanent Plan: Post-Permanency Reviews
statement: After a permanent plan is chosen, the child's case is reviewed at least every six months while the case stays open. Most reviews are in court. Some can be done by a county review panel, but the judge must do a review at least once a year. You can ask for the judge to do it.
source_name: WIC 366.3(d); Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.740(b); Judicial Council booklet p.18
source_says: may be conducted by the court or an appropriate local agency
steps: Confirmed after text is live with position() on full_content (pos 1). Searched public.law for WIC 366.3, opened it: (d) says 'the status of the child shall be reviewed at least every six months', review 'may be conducted by the court or an appropriate local agency', court must do it 'Upon the request of the child's parents or legal guardians' and when 'It has been 12 months since a review was conducted by the court.' Opened rule 5.740 (courts.ca.gov/cms/rules/index.cfm?linkid=rule5_740&title=five): 'by the court or by a local administrative review panel' and 'No less frequently than once every 12 months, the court must conduct a review'. Opened the booklet PDF p.18. Every claim checks out except 'Most reviews are in court.' Asked of the 366.3 page whether it says most reviews are by the court: no. Rule 5.740 and the booklet do not say it either. No source found for 'most'.
fix: After a permanent plan is chosen, the child's case is reviewed at least every six months while the case stays open. The judge or a county review panel can do the review. The judge must do a review at least once a year. A parent or the child can ask for the judge to do it.

title: Parental Rights in Dependency Court
statement: If your child is removed, the judge must order services to help you get your child back in most cases. The law lists 17 serious situations where the judge can say no to services. If you are a father the court has not yet named a presumed parent, the judge may order services but does not have to.

steps: Confirmed after text is live with position() on full_content (pos 125). Searched public.law for WIC 361.5 and opened it. Sentence 3 leaves out two conditions in (a): the judge may order services for a biological father only after paternity is found or shown, and only if the court decides services will benefit the child. A man who is only an alleged father is not covered by that sentence of the law.
fix: If your child is removed, the judge must order services to help you get your child back in most cases. The law lists 17 situations where the judge can say no to services. If you are the biological father but the court has not named you a presumed parent, the judge may order services if they will help your child. The judge does not have to. Ask your lawyer how to be named a presumed parent.

title: Educational Rights Holder (JV-535)
statement: The judge can do this only when it is needed to protect the child. Early in a case, the judge can do it for a short time if a parent cannot be found or is not able or willing to make school decisions.
source_says: The county placing agency has made diligent efforts to locate and secure the participation of the parent or guardian
steps: Confirmed after text is live with position() on full_content (pos 228). Sentence 1: opened WIC 361 on public.law: 'The limitations may not exceed those necessary to protect the child.' Holds. Sentence 2: opened WIC 319 on public.law and read (j)(1). The court may limit the right for a time only 'if all of the following conditions are found': (A) 'The parent or guardian is unavailable, unable, or unwilling to exercise educational or developmental services rights', (B) the county made diligent efforts to find and include the parent, and (C) 'The child's educational and developmental services needs cannot be met without the temporary appointment'. The entry gives only (A). The order ends at the disposition hearing or when the petition is dismissed.
fix: The judge can do this only when it is needed to protect the child. Early in a case, the judge can do it for a short time, but only if three things are true: the parent cannot be found or is not able or willing to make school decisions, the county tried hard to find and include the parent, and the child's school needs cannot be met any other way.

Opened WIC 903.45: at the close of the disposition hearing the court orders the parent to see the county financial evaluation officer about ability to pay. Opened rule 5.534(c): counsel is 'subject to a claim by the court or the county for reimbursement as provided by law'.

title: School Rights for Children in Foster Care
statement: Education Code §§48853.5, 49069.5, 51225.2; WIC §361(a); Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.650
source_name: Education Code 48853.5, 49069.5, 51225.2; WIC 361(a)(1); Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.650
source_says: The new school shall immediately enroll the foster child ... shall provide all records to the new school within two business days.
steps: Confirmed after text is live with position() on legal_reference (pos 1). Read the page's full_content, then opened every cited item. Ed. Code 48853.5 (public.law): (c) 'Each local educational agency shall designate a staff person as the educational liaison for foster children.'; (f)(1) school of origin; (f)(8)(B) immediate enrollment; (f)(8)(C) new school's liaison contacts the last school 'Within two business days' and the last school sends records in two business days. title: The Investigation: What Happens Before Court
statement: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents; WIC §§305, 309, 313, 328; Penal Code §11174.3
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents; WIC 305, 309, 313, 328; Penal Code 11174.3
source_says: the social worker shall immediately make any investigation the social worker deems necessary
steps: Confirmed after text is live with position() on legal_reference (pos 1). Read the page's full_content, then opened every cited item. Self-help guide (selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/juvenile-dependency/guide-parents): school interview without a court order when no police officer is present, and the worker must tell the parent afterward. WIC 305 (public.law): 'Any peace officer may, without a warrant, take into temporary custody a minor'. WIC 309: worker 'shall immediately release the child to the custody of the child's parent' unless listed conditions exist; relative assessed if 'available and requests emergency placement'. WIC 313(a): release 'within 48 hours after having been taken into custody, excluding nonjudicial days' unless a petition is filed. WIC 328: investigation and possible offer of child welfare services. Penal Code 11174.3(a): interview at school with a staff member of the child's choice. Each supports a part of the page.

title: The Jurisdiction Hearing
statement: WIC §§334, 355, 355.1, 356; Cal. Rules of Court, rules 5.682 and 5.684; Judicial Council, Juvenile Dependency Court and You
source_name: WIC 334, 355, 355.1, 356; Cal. Rules of Court rules 5.682, 5.684; Judicial Council booklet p.9
source_says: The parent or guardian may elect to admit the allegations of the petition or plead no contest
steps: Confirmed after text is live with position() on legal_reference (pos 1). Read the page's full_content, then opened every cited item. WIC 334, 355, 355.1 and 356 on public.law: hearing dates, preponderance standard, the injury presumption, and dismissal if not proved. Rule 5.682 on courts.ca.gov: admit, no contest, or 'submit the jurisdictional determination to the court based on the information provided to the court'. Rule 5.684: 'If the parent or guardian denies the allegations of the petition, the court must hold a contested hearing'; 'by a preponderance of the evidence'; if not proved 'the court must dismiss the petition and terminate any detention orders relating to the petition'. Booklet PDF p.9: 'the judge will decide whether the allegations in the petition are true.' Each supports a part of the page.
